title: 2008 AMC 12B Problem 9
statement: Points \(A\) and \(B\) are on a circle of radius \(5\) and \(AB = 6.\) Point \(C\) is the midpoint of the minor arc \(AB.\) What is the length of the line segment \(AC?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(O\) be the center and \(D\) the point where \(\overline{OC}\) meets \(\overline{AB}.\) Since \(C\) is the midpoint of arc \(AB,\) \(\overline{OC}\) is the perpendicular bisector of the chord, so \(AD = 3.\)

In right triangle \(ADO,\) \(OD = \sqrt{5^2 - 3^2} = 4,\) so \(DC = OC - OD = 5 - 4 = 1.\)

Then in right triangle \(ADC,\) \(AC = \sqrt{AD^2 + DC^2}\) \(= \sqrt{3^2 + 1^2}\) \(= \sqrt{10}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: The radius through the arc midpoint \(C\) perpendicularly bisects chord \(AB,\) meeting it at \(D\) with \(AD = 3\)
Find the center-to-chord distance \(OD,\) then \(DC = 5 - OD,\) and apply the Pythagorean theorem to \(\triangle ADC\)
